why.claim: Proton pump inhibitors like pantoprazole are the main medicines used long-term to calm the extra stomach acid that can happen in short bowel syndrome.

All oral proton pump inhibitors have an enteric coating, so how well they are absorbed may be limited in short bowel syndrome. If an oral one is not working early after surgery, trying an intravenous (IV) one is reasonable.
This product is a delayed-release tablet.
The label says the tablet is enteric-coated, so the body only starts absorbing pantoprazole after the tablet leaves the stomach.
